How to sleep well
in a noisy city
Use good earplugs. Soft foam ones that fit properly block most traffic and neighbour noise. Try a few types until you find the right one.
Add steady background sound. A fan or white noise covers sudden noises like sirens or doors slamming. It's cheap and simple.
Make the room as dark as possible. City lights sneak in. Blackout curtains or a sleep mask make a big difference.
Keep the same bedtime. A regular rhythm helps your body fall asleep faster, even when the city is still awake.
Wind down with something calm. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and it helps me switch off from the city noise.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It helps me switch off from the city noise.

slides.texte_overlay: Move your bed away from the window. Even a metre further from the street can make the room much quieter. Try it tonight.
Keep the bedroom cool. A slightly cold room helps deep sleep. Use a fan if you can't open the window. Cool and calm.
